key: None, verily, hath ever let or hindered this the most wise God’s mighty deed of magic, Whereby with all their flood, the lucid rivers fill not one sea wherein they pour their waters.
s: Before the hymn to Varuna turns to pleas for pardon, the singer marvels at the sea; Sāyaṇa, on 5.85.6, takes the magic as wisdom, and the deed as fitly Varuna’s, since the Supreme Lord abides in the forms of Varuna and the other gods.

evidence.words: “कवितमस्य प्रकृष्टप्रज्ञस्य “देवस्य द्योतमानस्य स्तुत्यस्य वा वरुणस्य “इमां सर्वप्रसिद्धां “महीं महतीं "मायां प्रज्ञां … इदं वरुणस्य महत् कर्म इति । अत्र अन्तरिक्षविस्तारादि समुद्रापूरणपर्यन्तं कर्म परमेश्वरस्यैवोचितं न वरुणस्येति न वाच्यं तस्य वरुणादिरूपावस्थानात् । एष ब्रह्मेत्यादिश्रुतेः ॥
evidence.gloss: Of the most wise (kavitama: of surpassing wisdom) god Varuṇa, shining or praiseworthy, this universally known, great māyā, that is, wisdom (prajñā) … This is Varuṇa’s great deed. Here it must not be said that the deed, from spreading the mid-air to not filling the sea, befits the Supreme Lord alone and not Varuṇa, because He abides in the forms of Varuṇa and the rest, by the śruti ‘this is Brahman’ and the like.

reason: The problem holds: “the works” had no antecedent; Sāyaṇa speaks of one karman, Varuṇa’s great deed (idaṃ varuṇasya mahat karma), the deed from spreading the mid-air to the unfilled sea (antarikṣavistārādi samudrāpūraṇaparyantaṃ karma), which he says must not be denied to Varuṇa since the Supreme Lord abides in the forms of Varuṇa and the rest (na vācyaṃ tasya varuṇādirūpāvasthānāt). Only “works” changed to “deed”, as the fix asks. Evidence re-cut verbatim from packet.js veda 56 --verse 5.85.6. Wilson’s note inverts Sāyaṇa (drops na vācyam) and is not relied on.
